findings.title: Spawned flushers never pass the new kill guard
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. These are not instances of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context Process class), so this guard is false for production workers. When a worker is declared hung, it is no longer killed before its replacement starts, and its handle is overwritten. If the old worker resumes, both workers can flush the same shards concurrently and produce duplicate segments; repeated hangs also leak workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the explicit SpawnProcess type and kill/reap the old worker before replacing it.

findings.title: Clean up every worker even after the join deadline expires
findings.body: When the join deadline expires, this break skips all remaining workers without terminating them. This occurs if next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier flusher takes the remaining time. Setting stopped only requests cooperative shutdown, so workers blocked in Redis or Kafka can remain alive across a rebalance while a new strategy starts replacement flushers. The timeout should limit waiting, not cleanup: terminate and reap all remaining workers when the deadline is exhausted, using a type check that recognizes SpawnProcess.
